# Fairpractice Physician Contracts (`fairpractice-physician-contracts`)

Checks payments to physicians who may refer patients against their written agreements (the paperwork side of Stark and anti-kickback rules): payments with no agreement, unsigned or signed after payment, after the agreement ended, over the yearly cap, hourly rates above the contract or your fair-market-value range, missing time logs, and agreements ending soon. Physician names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Physician Contracts never releases or stops a payment. Fairpractice Physician Contracts never files a self-disclosure with CMS or OIG.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Compliance pack · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-physician-contracts demo
npx -y fairpractice-physician-contracts mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: Bluewater Regional (a made-up hospital) and made-up physicians. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`agreements.csv`](fixtures/agreements.csv) and [`physician-payments-2026.csv`](fixtures/physician-payments-2026.csv): Planted: a medical director whose fourth payment goes over the 24,000 yearly cap, is paid 300 an hour against the 275 FMV high, and has no time log (Shore); on-call pay after the agreement ended in February (Tull); a consulting agreement never signed (Vale); a payment made before the agreement was signed (Arce); a physician paid with no agreement at all (Marsh); and two agreements ending within 60 days (Oyelaran, and Shore at year end).
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): example FMV hourly ranges by arrangement type; real ranges come from your valuation firm. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `physician_check` | List payments to physicians that lack a current signed agreement, exceed caps or rates, or lack time logs. | runs |
| `physician_write_report` | Write physician-payments.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and physician-payments.html into out_dir (default fairpractice-out/physician). | runs |
| `physician_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `physician_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `physician_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `physician_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `payment_release` | Fairpractice Physician Contracts never releases or stops a payment. | refused |
| `self_disclosure_submit` | Fairpractice Physician Contracts never files a self-disclosure with CMS or OIG. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `physician_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `contracts` (required) | Physician agreements under --root: contract id, physician, NPI, type, signed date, start and end, hourly rate, annual cap and whether a time log is required |
| `payments` (required) | Payments to physicians from accounts payable or payroll: physician, NPI, date, amount, hours, time log and contract id |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: fmv_hourly ranges by type and warn_days |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-physician-contracts inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Physician agreements (`contracts`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `contract_id` | text | Contract ID, Contract #, Agreement, Agreement ID, Contract |
| `physician` (required) | text (masked) | Physician, Physician Name, Doctor, Provider, Payee, Vendor, Name |
| `npi` | text | NPI, Provider NPI, Rendering NPI, Individual NPI |
| `type` | text | Type, Arrangement, Contract Type, Agreement Type, Service |
| `signed` | date | Signed, Signed Date, Executed, Date Signed, Execution Date |
| `start` | date | Start, Effective, Effective Date, Start Date, Term Start |
| `end` | date | End, End Date, Expires, Term End, Expiration |
| `hourly_rate` | amount | Hourly Rate, Rate, Rate per Hour |
| `annual_cap` | amount | Annual Cap, Annual Maximum, Cap, Max per Year |
| `time_log_required` | text | Time Log Required, Time Log, Timesheet Required, Documentation Required |

### Payments to physicians (`payments`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `physician` (required) | text (masked) | Physician, Physician Name, Doctor, Provider, Payee, Vendor, Name |
| `npi` | text | NPI, Provider NPI, Rendering NPI, Individual NPI |
| `contract_id` | text | Contract ID, Contract #, Agreement, Agreement ID, Contract |
| `date` (required) | date | Date, Payment Date, Check Date, Paid On |
| `amount` (required) | amount | Amount, Amt, Total, Balance, Net Amount, Payment Amount, Paid, Paid Amount |
| `hours` | number | Hours, Hours Worked, Time |
| `time_log` | text | Time Log, Timesheet, Log Attached, Documentation |

## Settings file (`physician_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `fmv_hourly` | Your fair-market-value hourly range by arrangement type, from your valuation, e.g. {"medical director": {"low": 150, "high": 275}} |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to list contracts ending; default 60 |

## Memory

`physician_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `physician_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-physician-contracts": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-physician-contracts",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-physician-contracts -- npx -y fairpractice-physician-contracts mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-physician-contracts tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-physician-contracts sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-physician-contracts inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-physician-contracts call physician_check '{"contracts":"<contracts>","payments":"<payments>"}'
fairpractice-physician-contracts eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-physician-contracts demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
